title: Tinker quiet-period cadence throttle + strategic pre-flight gate — tinker is the #1 daily-cost agent and the only Opus analytical agent omitted from the 2026-06-23 quiet-period sweep
headline_recommendation: Throttle dome-tinker from daily (`30 3 * * *`) to every-other-day during the quiet period (Recommendation A, immediate, ~$6.4/day / ~50% saving, 1-line reversible cron change), mirroring the 2026-06-23 operator sweep that throttled every other Opus analytical agent but missed tinker. Separately, evaluate a Haiku/script pre-flight gate + reduced-cadence Opus deep-dive as the permanent structural fix (Recommendation B, deferred, modeled on PROP-034/PROP-038).
executive_summary: Mode 3 real-cost analysis (PROP-101 data, 14d window) shows tinker is the single most expensive agent in the pipeline at p50 $12.77/run (sum $214.34/14d) — above curmudgeon ($10.28) and analyst ($9.40), the agents that do the actual analytical heavy-lifting. Tinker is the meta-ops agent whose explicit mandate includes 'Audit yourself. You are not exempt.' The 2026-06-23 quiet-period throttle reduced analyst/curmudgeon/decider/analyst-baby to 1/day, paused curmudgeon-verify, and cut workspace-sync/dome-mirror to 3 slots — but dome-tinker was left at daily 03:30 Opus. With the dome at day 72 of manual drought and the entire upstream chain at 1/day, a daily Opus tinker run that on most days produces 'pipeline GREEN' is the largest uncut single cost in the quiet pipeline.

recommendation_A_immediate.summary: Throttle dome-tinker to every-other-day during the quiet period.
recommendation_A_immediate.change: dome-tinker cronExpression: `30 3 * * *` -> `30 3 */2 * *` (every other day at 03:30 local). Update the task description to record the quiet-period throttle and revert trigger, matching the wording style of the other 2026-06-23 throttle notes.
recommendation_A_immediate.estimated_saving: ~$12.77 every other day saved => ~$6.4/day, ~$45/week, ~50% of tinker spend.
recommendation_A_immediate.risk: LOW. The PROP-030 backlog-trend pre-flight (cheap insurance against silent backlog growth) and the Mode 1/2 staleness+disk checks still run on every day tinker DOES run. During a genuine quiet period (no new content, upstream all 1/day, low churn), incident risk is structurally lower than during active periods, so doubling worst-case tinker-detection latency from 1d to 2d is acceptable.
recommendation_A_immediate.revert_trigger: Revert to `30 3 * * *` if the dome breaks its manual drought, if open_issues_total climbs back above ~50, if any Mode 1/2 red flag recurs across consecutive runs, or if the broader pipeline reverts off quiet-period cadence.
recommendation_A_immediate.authority: Operator-domain. The 2026-06-23 throttles were operator decisions; tinker should NOT self-modify its own schedule autonomously (and this scheduled run does not authorize schedule write-actions). Operator applies via update_scheduled_task or the schedule skill.

recommendation_B_strategic_deferred.summary: Permanent structural fix: a cheap (Haiku or script-only) pre-flight gate that runs all mechanical tinker checks, escalating to a full Opus run only when judgment is needed.
recommendation_B_strategic_deferred.rationale: Essentially every tinker pre-flight is already mechanical/scriptable: PROP-030 backlog metrics, prop-auto-close (PROP-102) walker, directive-auto-close (PROP-108) walker, operator-directive discovery, Mode 0 assigned-to-tinker scan, and the Mode 1/2 staleness/disk/FUSE quick-checks. Opus judgment is only required for (a) a found directive/Mode-0 item, (b) a Mode 1/2 red flag, or (c) a scheduled Mode 3 deep-dive. A Haiku/script gate could do the mechanical sweep daily and only spin up Opus on (a)/(b)/(c).
recommendation_B_strategic_deferred.precedent: Directly mirrors PROP-034 (split analyst into Sonnet-baby BAU-drain + Opus deep) and PROP-038 (split curmudgeon into Opus-discovery + Sonnet-verify). The model-split / cheap-gate pattern is proven in this pipeline.
recommendation_B_strategic_deferred.deep_dive_cadence: Run the full Opus Mode 3 deep-dive on a reduced cadence (e.g. every 3rd day) rather than daily; the gate handles liveness on the other days.
recommendation_B_strategic_deferred.why_deferred: Recommendation A captures ~50% of the saving immediately with a 1-line reversible change and zero new code. Recommendation B is multi-phase engineering (new gate prompt/script, dispatcher rework, model wiring) and should be scheduled when the drought ends or as a deliberate permanent-efficiency project, not rushed under quiet-period conditions.

counter_argument.for_keeping_daily: Tinker's daily run is cheap insurance against the disk-fill and backlog-growth incidents that have caused real damage (2026-05-07/08 disk cascade, 2026-05-09 near-miss, 2026-05-21 workspace-sync disaster). PROP-030 exists specifically because three consecutive 'GREEN' runs missed a backlog growing past 230 items. Halving tinker cadence doubles worst-case detection latency for exactly the class of problem tinker was built to catch.
counter_argument.rebuttal: Two mitigations make every-other-day acceptable during the quiet period specifically: (1) the daily dome-integrity run (02:00) independently surfaces site-health and build-drift, and each clone-using agent runs its own clone-hygiene preclean, so disk and structural signals are not solely tinker-dependent; (2) incident risk correlates with churn, and a manual-drought quiet period is the lowest-churn regime — the very conditions under which the operator already judged it safe to throttle every OTHER Opus agent. The revert trigger restores daily cadence the moment activity returns. Net: Recommendation A is the symmetric completion of a throttle the operator clearly intended pipeline-wide and simply missed for tinker.
counter_argument.against_recommendation_B: A Haiku/script gate adds a new failure surface (the gate mis-classifying a run as no-op and skipping a needed Opus deep-dive) and new maintenance burden. The analyst/curmudgeon splits required several follow-up PROPs to stabilize. Recommendation B should not be undertaken lightly; Recommendation A is strictly safer and reversible.

what_NOT_to_do: Do NOT have tinker self-modify its own cron in an autonomous scheduled run — schedule changes are operator-domain and this task file does not authorize schedule write-actions.
Do NOT skip the PROP-030 backlog-trend pre-flight on the days tinker runs; the insurance metric must still land every actual run.
Do NOT pursue Recommendation B before Recommendation A — A captures most of the value with none of the engineering risk.
Do NOT throttle below every-other-day (e.g. to weekly) during the quiet period; that would let backlog-trend blind spots reopen of the kind PROP-030 was built to close.

cost_analysis.recommendation_B_additional_saving: Variable; could push effective tinker cost toward the cheap-gate floor (~$1-2 on no-op days) on non-deep-dive days, but requires engineering investment.
cost_analysis.measurement_followup: After Recommendation A applies, the next tinker run lands on day N+2; PROP-101 self_cost rows confirm realized saving. Re-evaluate Recommendation B at drought-end.
